source.title: Infinitely deep neural networks as diffusion processes

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own SGD training experiment and finds that the proposed reparameterized gradients train stably while standard gradients produce slow or divergent loss trajectories; this refines the claim by showing training behavior depends on parameterization and gradient treatment. It does not test CIFAR error or the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: Most results concern initialization-time distributions, diffusion limits, and function-space behavior, not training classification error. The only training result is the MNIST SGD comparison in Section 4.3. Cited prior-work findings and values used only to characterize the setup are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization-time function distributions and compares gradient parameterizations in identity ResNets on MNIST. These results do not test any listed version: preserving forward signals is not evidence of faster training in plain networks, and changing gradient parameterization is not an initialization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish diffusion limits for identity ResNets with suitable shrinking parameter distributions and activation assumptions, while cautioning that forward-propagation results do not automatically establish back-propagation properties or competitive performance. Their MNIST experiment favors reparameterized gradients under a shared learning rate.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies diffusion limits and a toy MNIST SGD experiment for identity ResNets; it does not test the original claim's CIFAR training-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training loss behavior changes with gradient parameterization; the standard-gradient trajectory is sensitive to the common learning rate across depth and width settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth-scaled parameter distributions yield identity-ResNet diffusion limits that retain input dependence and avoid perfect output correlation under the stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable depth-dependent parameter distributions preserve nondegenerate forward function distributions in identity ResNets at infinite depth.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST after one epoch, reparameterized gradients give stable loss decrease across tested depths and widths and 87.1–90.6% test accuracy; standard gradients with a shared tuned learning rate give slow or divergent trajectories and fail to exceed 72.4% accuracy uniformly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient parameterization affects whether a shared learning rate produces stable SGD training across the tested identity-ResNet depths and widths.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2020, PMLR Volume 108
record.problems: The training comparison is on MNIST and reports one epoch only. Training-loss values are primarily presented in a figure, with no numeric per-configuration losses in the text. No control or uncertainty estimates are reported for the training comparison, and the experiment does not measure training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying training results are reported. Initialization-time function samples and diffusion-limit properties do not measure training outcomes covered by the claim versions; cited findings from prior studies are excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe or size dependence.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth in plain networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.

Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth in plain networks, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and deep convolutional kernels. Forward-propagation distributions alone do not establish these effects.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to a measured threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable normalization-free training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification is unsupported: a result about parameterization does not qualify a version unless it measures that version's stated effect. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student local minima and student width.
Plain versus residual shortcut depth comparison, CIFAR-10/ImageNet training error, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian training speed, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Training above a stability limit, loss and curvature dynamics, and sharpness behavior.
Batch-normalization comparisons, accuracy speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

rows.measure: training loss trajectory; test accuracy after 1 epoch
rows.value: stable loss decrease over all considered values for L and D; average test accuracies after 1 epoch in the range [87.1%, 90.6%]
rows.note: The study gives a range across considered configurations, not individual configuration values in the text. Test accuracy is reported alongside the training-loss result; no training classification error is given.
rows.check: The reported stable loss decrease and 87.1–90.6% test accuracy are supported, but neither measures a listed version. This aggregate row also combines training loss and test accuracy across configurations.

rows.note: The result concerns optimization parameterization and training dynamics, not the claim versions' named benchmarks or classification-error outcomes.
rows.check: Slow or divergent trajectories under a shared learning rate do not measure a listed version. The 72.4% statement concerns failure to exceed that accuracy uniformly across configurations; it is not an accuracy ceiling for every configuration. The row combines distinct slow and divergent outcomes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
